Q: How to Debug Dynamics 365 Business Central ( Wave2 ) in a correct way? A:

As we know, Debugging refers to the process which involves discovering and resolving application errors. Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central on-prem debugging needs users to activate server-side debugging while they use Visual Studio Code with the AL Language extension. You need to configure launch.json by setting the request value to attach before you can publish your extension and press F5 to begin your session. After that you should perform actions in the web client which will activate the breakpoints. Debugging success requires proper server setup along with correct symbols and instance information.

By Sam Peterson - Dynamics Square

Q: PowerShell : how to zip directory based on file name A:

There is a problem if using $input in:

$input = [System.IO.File]::OpenRead($file.FullName)
$input.CopyTo($entry.Open())
$input.Dispose()

This is an automatic variable in PowerShell which's type is already defined:

$input.GetType() # System.Collections.ArrayList+ArrayListEnumeratorSimple

Your code might work using it but it's not recommended. If you were to inspect it, its content (a file stream in this case) would be gone... you should change it to something different.

$input = 'hello'
$input -eq 'hello' # True
$input             # As soon as you inspect it, there is nothing

The main issue is where you're presumably trying create a entry for the folder having the same name as the XML (TEST123 in the example), there is no such thing as [System.IO.Path]::OpenRead(...) and opening a stream for a directory isn't a thing in .NET; even if it did, Stream.CopyTo(Stream) wouldn't handle the recursive copy of the contents of that folders and you're also not handling the zip entry creation for each child item in that directory.

The easiest way to solve your issue with a .NET API is to use ZipFile.CreateFromDirectory, it doesn't have the 2GB limitation:

foreach ($file in $files) {
    try {
        # Create the destination zip path (same folder, same name, .zip extension)
        $zipPath = Join-Path $sourceDir ($file.BaseName + '.ZIP')

        [System.IO.Compression.ZipFile]::CreateFromDirectory(
            $file.DirectoryName, # DirectoryName is the absolute path of the parent directory
            $zipPath,
            [System.IO.Compression.CompressionLevel]::Optimal
            $false)              # Don't include base directory

        Write-Host "Zipped '$($file.Name)' to '$zipPath'"

    }
    catch {
        Write-Error "Failed to zip '$($file.Name)': $_"
    }
}

Using the argument includeBaseDirectory set to $false your zip archive should become:

TEST123.ZIP
├── TEST123.XML
└── TEST123
    └── etc...

Another option is to use Compress-ZipArchive, I made this cmdlet specifically to overcome the 2GB limitation while having a similar usage as Compress-Archive.

If going this route, install the module first:

Install-Module PSCompression -Scope CurrentUser

Then the loop logic is very simple:

foreach ($file in $files) {
    try {
        # Create the destination zip path (same folder, same name, .zip extension)
        $zipPath = Join-Path $sourceDir ($file.BaseName + '.ZIP')

        # \* = Compress the contents of this folder but not the folder itself
        Compress-ZipArchive "$($file.DirectoryName)\*" -Destination $zipPath -ErrorAction Stop
        Write-Host "Zipped '$($file.Name)' to '$zipPath'"

    }
    catch {
        Write-Error "Failed to zip '$($file.Name)': $_"
    }
}

Q: Could not open JPA EntityManager for transaction problem after reconnecting to DB A:

The problem is test-on-borrow and validation.query are not valid HikariCP properties those belong to older pools like DBCP/c3p0. HikariCP silently ignores them so your connection never gets validated before use.

Replace with the correct HikariCP properties:

properties

spring.datasource.hikari.connection-test-query=SELECT 1
spring.datasource.hikari.keepalive-time=30000

Also your pool config has a conflict minimum-idle=15 but maximum-pool-size=10. Minimum can't exceed maximum. Fix that too:

properties

spring.datasource.hikari.minimum-idle=5
spring.datasource.hikari.maximum-pool-size=10
spring.datasource.hikari.keepalive-time=30000
spring.datasource.hikari.connection-test-query=SELECT 1

keepalive-time periodically pings idle connections so stale ones get evicted before your app tries to use them. That's what actually prevents the Connection is closed error after DB comes back up.

Q: Faster functions than lm() in R A:

For anyone else coming across this issue, I've created a package that acts as a wrapper for the excellent glm4() function in the 'MatrixModels' package, but adds convenient model methods and functions designed to mimic those associated with the glm() function from the 'stats' package, including summary() , anova(), etc etc.

You can find it on CRAN here: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/glm4/index.html
